original_title: Box Office: ‘Supergirl’ Sputters Overseas With $30 Million, ‘Jackass: Best and Last’ Limps to $1.9 Million Internationally
summary_en: DC Studios' new Supergirl film stumbled in its international debut, earning a modest $30 million. Meanwhile, Pixar's Toy Story 5 continues its reign at the top of the box office.
ai_analysis: This box office performance highlights the evolving landscape of tentpole releases, where established franchises still hold significant sway over new IP, even within the superhero genre.

en.title: Supergirl Sputters Overseas, Toy Story 5 Dominates Box Office
en.summary: DC Studios' new Supergirl film stumbled in its international debut, earning a modest $30 million. Meanwhile, Pixar's Toy Story 5 continues its reign at the top of the box office.
en.body:
The highly anticipated **Supergirl** film has failed to soar at the international box office, bringing in a disappointing $30 million from 77 markets. This figure represents a weak start for a tentpole of this magnitude, especially considering the global reach of DC Studios' superhero properties. The film also underperformed domestically, contributing to a worldwide debut that fell short of expectations. 

In stark contrast, Disney and Pixar's **Toy Story 5** continues to capture audiences' imaginations and wallets. Entering its second weekend, the beloved animated sequel pulled in an impressive $21 million domestically on Friday alone. Projections suggest it will add another $70 million to $80 million by Sunday, pushing its North American total towards a staggering $300 million. This enduring success underscores the power of nostalgia and consistent quality in family entertainment.

## Box Office Battleground

While **Supergirl** was expected to contend for the top spot, it found itself overshadowed by the continued popularity of **Toy Story 5**. Forecasts had placed **Supergirl**'s opening weekend in the $45 million to $50 million range domestically, with some optimistic predictions reaching higher. However, the film's international performance suggests a broader challenge in connecting with a global audience. Adding to the weekend's crowded releases, **Jackass: Best and Last** also saw a modest performance, earning $1.9 million internationally, further solidifying **Toy Story 5**'s dominance.

## Fan Reactions and Franchise Power

The disparity in box office performance is likely to spark conversations among fans about the current appetite for superhero films versus established, universally loved franchises. While **Supergirl** represents a new chapter for DC, its initial box office reception indicates a need for a strong critical and audience response to gain momentum. The robust performance of **Toy Story 5**, bolstered by a 93% score on Rotten Tomatoes and an "A" CinemaScore, demonstrates the lasting appeal of a franchise that consistently delivers heartwarming stories and memorable characters. The online buzz for **Supergirl** ranged from hopeful predictions of over a billion dollars to more tempered expectations, but the initial numbers suggest a steeper climb than anticipated.

## What's Next

All eyes will be on **Supergirl**'s second weekend performance to see if it can rebound and build word-of-mouth. Meanwhile, **Toy Story 5** is poised to continue its impressive box office run. Details regarding the international performance of **Jackass: Best and Last** beyond its initial $1.9 million will also be monitored.
